content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or corrections.
- Overestimates in the middle to late period when prices are trending upward or recovering — often overshooting the true peak.
- Shows strong lag in responding to recent price spikes; forecasts lag behind actual price movements by 5–10 days.
- Tends to overreact to minor volatility, creating artificial “noise” in forecasts that doesn’t reflect underlying trend.
- Mean reversion bias: forecasts often push prices back toward historical averages too aggressively, especially after sharp moves.
- Underestimates the magnitude of price rebounds after corrections — fails to capture “recovery momentum” in the 10–15 day window.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum; fails to account for policy or supply-side shocks that cause sudden price shifts.
- Forecasts are too smooth — underestimates volatility clustering and “price jumps” in the final 5–7 days of the horizon.
